rd.heading: Research and Development Expenses
rd.text:
Research and Development (“R&D”) has been, and will continue to be, central to our business model. Our R&D expenses to date have been primarily attributable to the development of our next-generation blood tests for early cancer detection, development of our multiomics platform, and clinical validation of our early colorectal cancer detection test. Our R&D expenses primarily include salaries and benefits, stock-based compensation expenses, direct research and development expenses (testing cost, pre-clinical and clinical trial costs including external R&D expenses incurred under arrangements with third parties), materials, laboratory supplies and equipment, information technology (including cloud computing and data storage, equipment and computer hardware costs, and software related expenses), facility costs (including rent, depreciation and amortization, repairs and maintenance and other facility related expenses), consulting, contractor costs, along with other expenses.

Payments, including non-refundable advance payments, made prior to the receipt of goods or services to be used in R&D activities are deferred and recognized as an expense in the period in which the related goods are received or services are rendered.

ga.heading: General and Administrative Expenses
ga.text:
Our general and administrative (“G&A”) expenses primarily consist of costs for our executive, accounting and finance, legal, human resources, marketing, and other administrative support functions. These expenses consist principally of personnel costs, including salaries, bonuses, fringe benefits, stock-based compensation expenses, and travel expenses, as well as professional services fees such as consulting, audit, tax, and legal fees, and general corporate costs and allocated overhead expenses.

We expect our general and administrative expenses to increase in future periods as we support the growth of our business, commercialize SimpleScreen CRC, expand our infrastructure and pursue commercialization of additional diagnostic test candidates, if approved. As a public company, we also expect to continue incurring expenses for accounting, audit, legal, regulatory and tax services; Nasdaq and SEC compliance; directors’ and officers’ insurance; investor relations; and other public-company requirements.

Stock-based compensation expense included in G&A expenses was $30.9 million and $34.0 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively. Of the $30.9 million recognized for the three-month period, $29.8 million related to converted RSUs for which the service conditions had been satisfied as of September 30, 2026.

nonop.heading: Interest expense
nonop.text: Interest expense increased by $0.5 million to $1.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, and by $8.3 million to $9.0 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared with $0.6 million in each prior-year period. The nine-month increase was primarily due to $7.7 million of non-cash interest expense and amortization of debt issuance costs. Interest expense on the Roche Convertible Note, which converted at the July 20, 2026 closing, was $0.8 million for the three months and $7.3 million for the nine months, including $2.1 million of coupon interest. Interest expense also included interest accrued on the Exact convertible note before its September 8, 2026 conversion. Neither note was outstanding at September 30, 2026.

net.text: Our net losses may fluctuate significantly from quarter-to-quarter and year-to-year, depending on the timing of regulatory approvals and R&D activities.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, net cash used in operating activities was $58.7 million, primarily attributable to our net loss of $72.5 million and $70.7 million of net cash used by changes in operating assets and liabilities, partially offset by net non-cash adjustments of $84.5 million. Non-cash adjustments primarily included stock-based compensation expense of $47.6 million, depreciation and amortization of $18.3 million, a loss on remeasurement of the convertible note of $11.7 million, non-cash interest expense and amortization of debt issuance costs of $7.7 million, and non-cash lease expense of $1.9 million, partially offset by net accretion and amortization of investments in marketable securities of $2.7 million.

Our R&D expenses to date have been primarily attributable to the development of our next-generation blood tests for early cancer detection, development of our multiomics platform, and clinical validation of our early colorectal cancer detection test. Our R&D expenses primarily include salaries and benefits, stock-based compensation expenses, direct research and development expenses (testing cost, pre-clinical and clinical trial costs including external R&D expenses incurred under arrangements with third parties), materials, laboratory supplies and equipment, information technology (including cloud computing and data storage, equipment and computer hardware costs, and software related expenses), facility costs (including rent, depreciation and amortization, repairs and maintenance and other facility related expenses), consulting, contractor costs, along with other expenses.

sbc.text: Stock-based compensation expense included in R&D was $11.0 million and $13.6 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively. Of the $11.0 million recognized for the three months ended September 30, 2026, $9.9 million related to converted RSUs for which the service conditions had been satisfied as of September 30, 2026. Incremental stock-based compensation expense in research and development related to the October 2025 option repricing was $0.2 million and $0.6 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively.

wc.text: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, net cash used in operating activities was $58.7 million, primarily attributable to our net loss of $72.5 million and $70.7 million of net cash used by changes in operating assets and liabilities, partially offset by net non-cash adjustments of $84.5 million. Non-cash adjustments primarily included stock-based compensation expense of $47.6 million, depreciation and amortization of $18.3 million, a loss on remeasurement of the convertible note of $11.7 million, non-cash interest expense and amortization of debt issuance costs of $7.7 million, and non-cash lease expense of $1.9 million, partially offset by net accretion and amortization of investments in marketable securities of $2.7 million. The $70.7 million of net cash used by changes in operating assets and liabilities primarily reflected a decrease of $31.7 million in deferred revenue, a decrease of $13.4 million in other long-term liabilities, an increase of $11.8 million in prepaid expenses and other current assets, an increase of $7.5 million in accounts receivable (including an $8.0 million receivable for the SBX platform delivery milestone from Roche), a decrease of $7.5 million in operating lease liabilities, and an increase of $1.9 million in inventory, partially offset by an increase of $4.0 million in accounts payable.

capex.text: Net cash used in investing activities was $124.5 million during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, and consisted of net purchases of marketable securities of $109.3 million ($271.6 million of purchases, partially offset by $162.3 million of proceeds from maturities) and $15.2 million used for the purchase of property and equipment.

net sales.heading: Revenue
net sales.text:
We recognize license and collaboration revenue in the United States under our exclusive license agreement with Exact, pursuant to which we granted exclusive commercialization rights, as well as development, data, and manufacturing and other licenses.

We also generate revenue from the sale and distribution of EarlyCDT Lung test kits in the United Kingdom and other international markets, royalties on EarlyCDT Lung tests performed, and the sale of EarlyCDT Lung test plates through our U.K.-based subsidiary, Freenome Ltd.

In addition, we generate revenue from diagnostic and research services performed using our proprietary multiomics platform under a Research Services Agreement with a related party.

Following FDA approval of SimpleScreen CRC in July 2026, the $100.0 million milestone under our agreement with Exact was earned and included in the transaction price. Exact paid the milestone on September 22, 2026. Based on the updated transaction price, we recognized approximately $182.5 million in revenue under the agreement during the three months ended September 30, 2026. This included $22.5 million cumulative catch-up adjustment to revenue recognized in the fourth quarter of 2025 and the six months ended June 30, 2026, and $2.5 million related to development services.

License and collaboration revenue.text: We recognize license and collaboration revenue in the United States under our exclusive license agreement with Exact, pursuant to which we granted exclusive commercialization rights, as well as development, data, and manufacturing and other licenses.

Service and other revenue.text: Cost of services reflects the aggregate costs incurred in delivering our products and services and is composed of material and service costs including personnel costs, cost of consumables, kits, contract maintenance, labor, and freight associated with the service and other revenue. Our cost of services will increase with commercialization of our products.

intro.text: Freenome is an early cancer detection company developing blood-based screening tests to identify cancer in its earliest, most treatable stages. The company’s proprietary AI-driven multiomics discovery platform analyzes circulating cell-free DNA methylation patterns at single-base resolution alongside additional biomarkers to detect multiple cancers. Freenome’s development of FDA-approved SimpleScreen CRC for colorectal cancer screening and a pipeline of tests for lung cancer and additional single- and multi-cancer indications is designed to increase cancer screening participation among millions of at-risk individuals.

s.t: Pursuant to the Business Combination Agreement, upon the closing of the Business Combination, (i) each share of redeemable convertible preferred stock of Legacy Freenome (on an as converted to common stock basis; see Note 9) and each share of common stock of Legacy Freenome, whether vested or unvested, was converted into 0.282895 shares of the Company’s common stock and (ii) each outstanding option to purchase common stock and each restricted stock unit of Legacy Freenome was converted into an option to purchase, or a restricted stock unit settleable in, shares of the Company’s common stock based on the Exchange Ratio, with corresponding adjustments to the exercise price of options.

Immediately prior to the closing of the Business Combination, all 212,541,832 issued and outstanding shares of the redeemable convertible preferred stock of Legacy Freenome were converted into 213,907,881 shares of Legacy Freenome’s common stock.
